- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.7) — model tends to be overly bullish.
- Underestimate when sentiment is low (e.g., <0.5) — model misses downward momentum or fails to anticipate sharp drops.
- Overshoot after recent spikes — model reacts too quickly to price surges, then overcorrects downward.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often forecasts prices to revert to recent 10-15 day averages, but true price often continues trending.
- Lagged response to sentiment shifts — model reacts 1-2 days after sentiment changes, especially when sentiment drops sharply.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently underestimate late-period price increases (especially >70) when sentiment is rising.
- Avoid smoothing out volatility — model tends to flatten sharp moves, especially when sentiment is volatile (e.g., 0.2–0.8 swings).
